sam (customer): hey team — hitting a weird streaming issue. endpoint returns first few tokens then connection sits in FIN_WAIT on our side, client never gets final event. curl shows 200 OK, then nothing for ~30s, then connection reset. We rotate auth tokens every 15s via our proxy. Repro steps: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

mia (support): sorry about that — can you paste the curl output with --trace-ascii and tell us region + model?

sam (customer): here's the truncated trace (sensitive bits redacted):
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (3.120.45.6) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
<
: chunked comment line\n 0000...
* state: TLSv1.3, cipher TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* about 30 seconds of silence here then TCP RST from peer
```
region: us-west-2, model: redwood-v1. We also send `X-Client-TTL: 15` to our auth proxy (it rotates tokens).

mia (support): ack — escalating to eng, thanks :thumbsup:

tom (eng-runtime): quick q — do you see any `100-continue` or extra headers? Is Transfer-Encoding chunked at the client? Also does the proxy actively close idle upstream connections? which client lib are you using?

sam (customer): node-fetch with a keepAlive agent. nginx fronts our auth service which performs the rotation. nginx config snippet on auth side: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";` We force upstream reconnects every 15s to pick up new tokens.

alex (eng-infra): got it. this smells like a token-swap + upstream connection closing sequence that leaves the server with a half-closed socket. if nginx sends `Connection: close` or forces a reset while the server has already started streaming, the client can end up with partial chunks and no final event. also possible TLS session renegotiation side-effects when you rotate mid-stream.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back streaming auth change at 13:10 UTC (2141598600) — potential impact window overlaps reported time. tagging @tom

tom (eng-runtime): thanks — we pushed a small change earlier that made auth middleware validate on first write. that caused a tiny comment frame to be emitted then we paused while awaiting auth. combined with upstreams that close on token rotation, it can leave the stream in limbo. short-term workaround: avoid rotating the upstream connection mid-stream (disable auth_proxy rotation) or ensure the proxy does not send `Connection: close` to upstreams. longer-term: we should not write any bytes to the client before token validation completes; if we need a heartbeat, emit server-side comment frames at a configured cadence instead of relying on auth-side writes.

mia (support): @sam — can you try a quick test: bypass the auth proxy for 1-2 minutes and call the same curl command. if stream completes that confirms the proxy rotation as the root cause. please also collect `curl -v` and a short tcpdump if possible.

sam (customer): testing now — bypassed proxy and hit the endpoint directly, stream completed fine. Rolling back the proxy rotation now and will retest in ~20m, will post results. thanks everyone.

mia (support): great, please update here. if it still fails after disabling rotation include the tcpdump and we'll escalate to an incident. :pray:
